raw_response:
I am old now, and with only 6 mu and just myself at home, I cannot make things too fancy. I still do the wheat-maize way because that is what I know, and it spreads the risk. Wheat gives me grain and steady yield, then maize follows right after, same as our county has done for years. I do not like cutting inputs too hard, because if the crop turns yellow or grows weak, the yield loss hurts more than saving a little money. But I also cannot spend wildly. So this year I will do the same basic way that has worked for me: wheat with base fertilizer plus one topdress, irrigate when the crop really needs it, then rush into summer maize right after wheat harvest with simple tillage and one more round of fertilizer. On 6 mu, one person can still manage, but I will rely on machine service for plowing and harvest timing when needed.
